headline: Ahead cumulatively, uneven year to year
summary: Peterborough reported 1,345 homes against a cumulative provincial target of 1,207 from 2023-2025 (111%). It exceeded target in 2023 and 2025 but reached 75% in 2024.
methodology_note: Housing-progress targets are a provincial measurement framework and should not be read as a direct measure of municipal planning productivity.

headline: Ridership has recovered from the 2023 level
summary: Reported total ridership rose from 3,205,294 in 2023 to more than 3.7 million in 2025 — a minimum increase of about 15.4%. A 2018 historical reference of 4,973,571 is shown, but 2025 is published only as a rounded lower bound, so no exact recovery-to-peak percentage is claimed.
methodology_note: Uses City-reported all-mode ridership. Comparability is stronger for 2023-2025 than for the older historical reference because service design and counting practices can change.

headline: Regional Crime Severity Index is lower than in 2021
summary: Statistics Canada’s Peterborough CMA CSI moved from 64.8 in 2021 to 57.3 in 2025, an 11.6% decline, with a small increase in 2024 before falling again in 2025. Lower is better.
methodology_note: The longitudinal series uses the Peterborough CMA for consistent boundaries. The separate PPS service-area CSI is retained as a current service-area metric and should not be spliced into the CMA trend.

headline: Current plan, old condition observation
summary: The City has a 2025 Asset Management Plan, but key road-condition observations still rely on 2023 asset-condition data. That is useful structural context, not a current 2026 outcome reading.
methodology_note: Infrastructure is intentionally excluded from the fresh-signal scorecard until a newer comparable network-condition observation is published. 2025 work delivered and funding-gap estimates remain available as context.

headline: Latest system count rose 16% in 2025
summary: The City reported a minimum of 932 people experienced homelessness in 2025, up from 803 in 2024 (+16%). The May 2026 shelter report also says demand continues to exceed the existing 127-bed emergency shelter/overnight system.
methodology_note: This is the freshest City-reported system-pressure indicator available. It counts people connected to services who were unsheltered, sheltered or couch surfing; it is not a point-in-time count and should not be compared directly with older RGI waitlist totals.
